marks.q: EBITDA guidance for 2022 is expected to be in the range of $70-$80m million, which remains in-line with market expectations, and is supported by the improved trading conditions.
We are pleased to be able to reconfirm our 2022 EBITDA guidance of US$ 70-80 million.
EBITDA for the year to 31 December 2022 is expected to be between US$70‐US$72m, which is within the previous guidance range given.

EBIDTA for the year ending Dec 31st 2022 is expected to be in line with the previously announced range of USD 70-72m, with EBITDA guidance for the year ending 31 December 2023 expected to be between US$75‐US$83m.
It is not yet clear how much of the outstanding Euro 4 million GMS will be able to recover, and therefore if any adjustment to 2022 guidance will be necessary.

Given the current high levels of utilisation secured, combined with higher day rates, the Group expects the financial performance to continue to improve and reiterates its EBITDA guidance of between US$ 75-US$ 83 million for 2023.

Given the current high levels of utilisation secured, combined with higher day rates, the Group expects the financial performance to continue to improve and reiterates its EBITDA guidance of between US$ 75-US$ 83 million for 2023.
We are now projecting a higher EBITDA than previously indicated and we are changing the EBITDA guidance for 2023 to be in the range of US$ 77 - 85 million.

Gulf Marine Services (GMS), a leading provider of self-propelled and self-elevating support vessels for the offshore oil, gas, and renewables sectors, is pleased to announce it now anticipates EBITDA in the range of US$83m to US$86m (previously: US$77m-US$85m) for the 12 months ending December 2023 and US$87m to US$95m for the 12 months ending December 2024.

Gulf Marine Services (GMS), a leading provider of self-propelled and self-elevating support vessels for the offshore oil, gas, and renewables sectors, is pleased to announce it now anticipates adjusted EBITDA to be approx. US$86m (previously: US$83m to US$86m) for the 12 months ended December 2023 and reconfirms its adjusted EBITDA guidance for the 12 months ending December 2024 at US$87m to US$95m.

Given the current high levels of utilisation secured, combined with higher day rates, the Group expects the financial performance to continue to improve and reiterates its adjusted EBITDA guidance for 2024 between US$ 92 million to US$ 100 million.
Given the Group's improved performance in H1 2024, we reaffirm our adjusted EBITDA guidance for 2024, projecting a range between US$ 92 million and US$ 100 million.

The Company is glad to revise its adjusted EBITDA guidance for 2024 to be in the range of USD 95 million to USD 100 million, versus the adjusted EBITDA guidance communicated earlier of USD 92 million to USD 100 million.
Adjusted EBITDA guidance for 2024 increased to be in the range of US$ 96 - 101 million.
For 2025, GMS expects adjusted EBITDA to reach USD 100-108 million, an increase from the previously forecasted 2025 EBITDA guidance of USD 92-100 million.

With 96% secured utilisation and improved day rates for 2025, we look forward to another year of strong financial performance with our adjusted EBITDA guidance for 2025 of between US$ 100.0 million and US$ 108.0 million.
Adjusted EBITDA guidance for 2025 remains in the range of US$ 100 - 108 million.
Adjusted EBITDA guidance for 2025 remains in the range of US$ 100 - 108 million.
GMS now expects 2025 adjusted EBITDA in the range of USD 101‐109 million, up from prior guidance of US$ 100-108 million.
GMS remains highly confident in achieving its increased Adjusted EBITDA guidance for 2025 of US$ 101 - 109 million (previously US$ 100 - 108 million) as well as our leverage target for the year.
Previously issued adjusted EBITDA guidance between US$ 105 million to US$ 115 million for 2026 is currently being assessed due to the ongoing geopolitical situation in the Gulf region.
We are also pleased to confirm that these developments are in line with our expectations, and we maintain our adjusted EBITDA guidance for 2026 in the range of USD 105 million to USD 115 million.

marks.q: Our adjusted EBITDA guidance between US$ 105 million to US$ 115 million for 2026 is maintained.

The Company is maintaining its adjusted EBITDA guidance for 2026 in the range of USD 105 million to USD 115 million but continues to assess the final financial impact of this disruption through ongoing discussions with its clients.
Despite H1 2026 operational disruptions, resulting from the conflict in the Gulf, performance is expected to rebound in H2 2026, assuming no return to active military actions.
We maintain our guidance for the Adjusted EBITDA for 2026 to be in the range of US$ 105 - 115 million, assuming the geopolitical situation doesn’t materially impact vessel utilization.
